title: Lark and Nibbles' Seed Surprise
markdown:
Sunbeams sliced the classroom windows into stripes of gold. Outside, birdsong tinkled, a topsy-turvy tune. Lark’s fingers tapped the pocket where a magnifying glass peeped out. Garden day. Beside them Nibbles the otter did a wiggle-dance, sleek brown fur gleaming, whiskers twitching.

“Ms. Rowan! Those empty corners are sad. They need colour.”

Rowan’s smile was morning-warm. “New flowers. But how do we get them to grow in the bare spots?”

Nibbles splashed his tail, droplets sparkling. “We plant them!” He tumbled head over tail.

“Sometimes nature does the planting. Plants have clever ways of spreading seeds. Let’s discover them.”

Out they dashed — Lark’s determined stride, Nibbles’ splashing energy. The school garden buzzed. The corners: brown dirt. Lark sighed. Empty.

A wispy white fluff drifted from a tall feathery plant, spun like a tiny dancer, landed on the dusty path. “A little parachute for a seed.”

Nibbles’ nose twitched. “It floated all the way. Wheee!” He nudged it.

Then a prickly seed, a tiny spiky ball, snagged on Nibbles’ damp fur as he wriggled past. “Tickly!” He tried to shake it. It clung, hitching a ride.

“Clinging for a lift.” Lark’s glass was already out.

Nearby a stream trickled. A smooth brown seed bobbed. “Traveling by water. A little seed boat.” Lark dipped a finger.

They dashed, pointed, peered. A secret delivery service. Lark giggled, thrilled.

Back at the corners they helped. Lark puffed fluffy seeds toward the empty spots. Nibbles wiggled until the prickly ones stuck, then shook them off near the beds. For the water-loving seeds, the bright red watering can — a sprinkle-shower to help them settle.

“We’ve helped them find new homes, like nature does.”

Rowan named it once: seed dispersal. Wind like tiny kites. Fur like Nibbles’. Water a gentle ride. She did not add a speech about clever tricks and racing off for more wonders.

Nibbles’ tail thumped. “That’s how new flowers pop up.”

Lark looked at the corners, no longer only sad: full of promise. They put the glass away. The dirt would do the next part without an announcement. Nibbles kept one prickly seed behind an ear until Rowan picked it off and set it, kindly, in a bare patch.
